title: Performance Tuning via Guesswork ("Streetlight Tuning")
damaged_code:
```ini
# /etc/sysctl.conf
# Copied blindly from a general forum post:
vm.swappiness = 0
vm.dirty_background_ratio = 5
```
pattern: Adjusting system metrics or runtime parameters (such as caching thresholds, page scan rates, or networking backlogs) based on trial-and-error internet recommendations.
why_bad: Can severely cripple actual performance. Advice valid for one system or kernel version may be completely inappropriate for another, or mask fixed bugs with permanent performance regressions.
detection: Arbitrary non-default values in system or database config files without documentation of corresponding baseline benchmarks, profiles, or workload assessments.
counterexample: Systematically benchmarking configurations sequentially, validating metrics after each change to verify impact.
fix: Establish a deliberate methodology: analyze performance, measure baselines, and test a limited set of parameters under exact target workloads.
source: Gregg, Brendan - *Systems Performance_ Enterprise and the Cloud* (2013, Pearson Education Limited (US titles)_Prentice Hall).pdf, Chapter 2.
